chapter_name: Chapter 01: The Sentence and Its Kinds
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will analyze sentence structures, confidently identify the four main kinds of sentences, and learn how to transform sentences from one kind to another without changing the meaning.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Welcome to Class 7! 🎉 You already know that sentences are groups of words making complete sense. But did you know sentences have different 'moods'? Sometimes they state facts, sometimes they give orders, and sometimes they shout with joy! Let's decode the secret moods of sentences.

lesson_modules.module_title: 🧱 Subject, Predicate, and Object (वाक्य के अंग)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Every sentence has a Subject (who/what does the action) and a Predicate (what is said about the subject). In Class 7, we also look for the Object—the noun/pronoun receiving the action of the verb.
examples_or_templates: The brave firefighter (Subject) rescued the trapped kitten (Predicate).

lesson_modules.module_title: 🎭 The Four Kinds of Sentences (वाक्यों के प्रकार)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Sentences are grouped by their purpose: Assertive/Declarative (states a fact), Interrogative (asks a question), Imperative (gives a command, request, or advice), and Exclamatory (expresses sudden, strong emotion).
examples_or_templates: Assertive: The library opens at 9 AM.
Interrogative: Why is the sky blue?
Imperative: Please submit your assignments by Friday.
Exclamatory: What a brilliant idea that is!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: We can change a sentence from one form to another. For example, changing an Assertive sentence into an Exclamatory one to add more emotion, or making a positive sentence negative.
examples_or_templates: Assertive -> Exclamatory: It is a very beautiful night. -> What a beautiful night it is!
Positive -> Negative: He is always on time. -> He is never late.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the kind of sentence: 'Never speak to strangers.'
❓ Which word is the Object in this sentence: 'The chef baked a delicious cake.'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Transform this Assertive sentence into an Interrogative sentence: 'You have finished reading the book.'
subjective_practice.hint: Move the helping verb to the beginning of the sentence.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Separate the Subject and Predicate in this sentence: 'Beyond the mountains lies a hidden valley.'
subjective_practice.hint: Ask yourself: 'What' lies beyond the mountains? (Sometimes the subject comes at the end!)

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this sentence into an Exclamatory sentence: 'The weather is extremely pleasant today.'
subjective_practice.hint: Start with 'How' or 'What a' and put an exclamation mark at the end.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎬 The Director's Chair
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Imagine you are directing a movie. Write 4 lines for your actors: One asserting a fact about a mystery, one asking a suspicious question, one commanding them to run, and one exclaiming in shock. Label the kind of sentence next to each!

chapter_summary: ⭐ A sentence consists of a Subject, a Predicate, and sometimes an Object.
⭐ There are four main kinds: Assertive (.), Interrogative (?), Imperative (.), and Exclamatory (!).
⭐ Sentences can be transformed from one type to another (e.g., Assertive to Exclamatory) to change the tone.
